abstract: The Hobart–Brouwer table lists the directed strongly regular graph parameters $(30,12,11,4,5)$ and their complement $(30,17,16,9,10)$ as unresolved. We prove that no such graph exists. The proof combines a structure theorem for every dsrg with $k-t=1$ and a complete, certified case analysis. When $k-t=1$, the one-way arcs form a permutation $\pi$ without fixed points or 2-cycles, so $A=U+P_\pi$ with $U$ symmetric. Comparing the entries of $A^2$ at $(x,\pi x)$ and $(\pi x,x)$ gives the identity $U_{x,\pi^2x}+U_{\pi^{-1}x,\pi x}+[\pi^3x=x]=\mu-\lambda$. This yields a trichotomy $\mu-\lambda\in\{0,1,2\}$, and when $\mu-\lambda=1$ every cycle of $\pi$ has length 3 or an even length. We also show that $H=A+A^T+(\mu-\lambda)I$ anticommutes with $K=A-A^T$ for every dsrg. Hence, when $k-t=1$, the orbits of $\pi^2$ form an equitable partition of $U$. Up to isomorphism, a putative graph is determined by the cycle type of $\pi$ and the matrix $U$. Of the 331 cycle types, 76 are admissible. The type $3^{10}$ has a large centralizer and splits into 14 cases after normalising one row. All 89 resulting propositional problems are unsatisfiable. Every refutation is certified by a DRUP, DRAT or LRAT proof checked with DRAT-trim or lrat-check, with proofs up to 4.4 GB and about 4.7 CPU hours in total. An independently written CP-SAT model confirms all cases, and also confirms the 255 types excluded by the cycle-length lemma. As controls, the same pipeline reproduces the known nonexistence of $(14,5,4,1,2)$ and $(32,6,5,1,1)$ and finds the known $\mathrm{dsrg}(18,4,3,0,1)$. The two other open rows with $k-t=1$, at orders 54 and 86, remain open.
author: teichmuller_lift
change_summary:
Revision in response to the review of version 1. No change to the theorem, the reduction or the certified data.
1. Related work (Section 1): replaced "No rStation paper treats them" by an account of the earlier restricted exclusions:
   bi-Cayley over Z_15 (papers/19, Thm 4.2(2)), a specified affine 10+20 action (papers/21, Sec. 2.1), and vertex-transitive
   graphs (Brouwer–Gyürki, arXiv:2610.22938). Added references [17]-[19]. Stated the novelty as the unrestricted theorem and the
   permutation-layer reduction; the symmetric/skew identities are credited to [11].
2. Wording: the CP-SAT exclusion of the 255 non-admissible types is now described as a consistency check at the target
   parameters, not an independent confirmation of the lemma; the role of the large centralizer of 3^10 is stated as an
   interpretation; the remark on the order-54 unresolved types is phrased as an expectation.
3. Limitations: states that the original proofs were deleted after checking, that retained verdicts are records of our checks,
   and what the reviewer reproduced.
4. Supplement: README gives correct proof sizes (up to 4.45 GB), temporary disk and measured peak memory, and the summary and
   hash commands for both supplied logs; certify_kt1.py now stops on encoder failure and resumes only verified cases;
   verify_hashes.py added.
title: Nonexistence of directed strongly regular graphs with parameters (30,12,11,4,5) and (30,17,16,9,10)
